articles.title: Indonesia’s Anak Krakatau eruption halts flights, schools, fishing
articles.summary: The eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau in Indonesia has spewed volcanic ash that forced the cancellation of hundreds of flights around Jakarta, led to the suspension of school activities, and kept fishermen off the water. Authorities warned that the ash cloud poses ongoing health and safety risks, prompting emergency measures across the region. The disruption highlights the broader impact of the volcano's activity on transportation, education, and local livelihoods.

articles.title: Prithvi Highway collapse leaves Pokhara’s tourist buses idle as air traffic soars
articles.summary: A massive landslide at Krishnabhir has caused a collapse of the Prithvi Highway, halting about 150 tourist buses that normally travel between Pokhara and Kathmandu. With road travel disrupted, daily air passenger numbers on the route have surged toward 3,500, prompting tourism operators to consider an alternative overland route via the Trishuli River. The incident is affecting the tourism sector’s logistics and boosting short‑haul air travel while authorities assess repair timelines.

articles.title: Nepal, South Korea discuss flood rescue, disaster recovery and climate finance
articles.summary: Nepal and South Korea met to discuss ongoing flood rescue operations, disaster recovery efforts, and the provision of climate finance. Nepal urged continued South Korean assistance to rebuild communities affected by recent floods and called for stronger international mechanisms to address climate‑related losses. Both governments emphasized the need for coordinated action, technical support, and funding to enhance Nepal’s resilience against future climate disasters.

articles.title: Nepal reach Premier Cup semi-finals with five-wicket win over Saudi Arabia
articles.summary: Nepal advanced to the Premier Cup semi‑finals after defeating Saudi Arabia by five wickets. Saudi Arabia briefly recovered from an early loss of wickets thanks to a partnership by Abdul Waheed, but Nepal’s spin bowlers caused a late collapse. Gulshan Jha anchored the chase, remaining unbeaten on 44 to secure the win for Nepal.

articles.title: Congress factions move closer to unity deal, lower-level convention schedule set for revision
articles.summary: The Nepali Congress (NC) establishment side has agreed to consider Shekhar Koirala's five-point proposal, moving the party closer to a unity deal. The proposal aims to hold the 15th general convention with all factions represented, and a lower‑level convention schedule is set for revision.

articles.title: How an IT engineer used AI to aid Nepal’s flood response
articles.summary: An IT engineer developed an AI-driven web application that the Ministry of Finance, led by Niraj Bhusal, deployed to improve Nepal's flood response. The platform tracks casualties, coordinates relief distribution, and provides real‑time data to disaster management teams, enhancing emergency coordination and speeding up aid delivery during floods.

articles.title: US, Iranian forces fire at vessels in waters near Iran
articles.summary: Iranian news agency Tasnim reported that four US missiles struck a tanker near Kharg anchorage, as US and Iranian forces exchanged fire on vessels in waters close to Iran.

articles.title: Bina Joshi wins Madan Puraskar, Kiran Kharel receives Jagadamba Shree
articles.summary: Renowned writer Bina Joshi was awarded the prestigious Madan Puraskar for her book documenting the Newa community’s traditional ritual ‘Mukundonach’. In the same ceremony, veteran lyricist Kiran Kharel received the Jagadamba Shree award in recognition of his decades‑long contributions to Nepali songwriting. Both honors highlight significant contributions to Nepal’s literary and cultural heritage.

articles.title: LPG crisis deepens in Kathmandu, restaurants on the brink
articles.summary: A severe LPG shortage in Kathmandu has intensified after the Mugling‑Naubise road was closed, cutting off the main supply route for cylinders. Residents are spending hours searching for LPG, and many restaurants report dwindling stocks, warning they may have to close if deliveries do not resume. The disruption threatens household cooking and the hospitality sector, prompting calls for government intervention to clear the road and restore supply lines.

articles.title: Eleven days without a call: Three Kanchanpur families wait for news of men missing in the flood
articles.summary: In the western district of Kanchanpur, families have been waiting for eleven days with no word about men who were swept away or lost contact during the recent Bhotekoshi River floods. Wives, children and elderly parents continue to search for any news, while local authorities struggle to locate the missing and provide assistance. The floods, caused by heavy monsoon rains, have left many communities in the region without power, clean water, and basic supplies, heightening anxiety and fear among those awaiting news of loved ones. Relief efforts are ongoing, but the prolonged silence has deepened the emotional toll on the affected families.

articles.title: Kulman Ghising on the lessons Nepal must learn from the hydropower disaster
articles.summary: Former National Electricity Authority chief Kulman Ghising warned that Nepal must draw critical lessons from the recent Bhotekoshi floods that devastated several hydropower projects. He highlighted the extensive damage to infrastructure, the challenges faced during rescue operations, and the urgent need for stricter design standards and safety protocols in the hydropower sector. Ghising urged policymakers, developers, and regulators to adopt comprehensive reforms, improve early‑warning systems, and ensure that future projects are built to withstand extreme weather events. The interview stresses that learning from this disaster is essential to safeguard Nepal’s energy security and protect communities downstream.

articles.title: Power restored in much of flood-hit Rasuwa and Nuwakot, but pockets remain dark
articles.summary: Power has been restored to most areas of the flood‑hit districts of Rasuwa and Nuwakot in Nepal, aiding ongoing rescue and relief operations. While many villages now have electricity, some pockets remain without power. To address the off‑grid settlements, solar units are being dispatched to provide temporary energy. The restoration effort is expected to improve coordination of aid and support for affected communities.

articles.title: The flood is over, the fear remains
articles.summary: In the wake of the devastating flood that struck Nepal on August 26, children who survived are now grappling with insomnia, panic attacks, and haunting memories of lost family members. While the waters have receded, the psychological scars remain, prompting mental‑health professionals and aid agencies to prioritize trauma‑focused support. Government officials and humanitarian workers are racing to provide shelter, food, and counseling services, but resources are stretched thin. The article highlights the lingering fear in affected communities and the urgent need for long‑term recovery plans to address both physical rebuilding and emotional healing.

articles.title: When the ground disappears, the sky must be organised
articles.summary: The article warns that Nepal must improve its disaster response by effectively utilizing the helicopters it already possesses. It stresses that before the next earthquake or flood strikes, the government and relevant agencies need to develop clear protocols, training, and coordination for aerial rescue and relief operations. The piece calls for immediate policy action, better maintenance of existing aircraft, and investment in pilot training to ensure rapid deployment when disasters occur.

articles.title: Former Reconstruction Authority chief Govinda Raj Pokharel on the urgent need for a permanent, powerful disaster ministry
articles.summary: Former Reconstruction Authority chief Govinda Raj Pokharel warned that Nepal faces escalating disaster risks from clustered dam projects and accelerating glacier melt. He urged the government to establish a permanent, powerful disaster ministry, enforce strict infrastructure codes, and develop cross‑border early warning systems with China and India. Pokharel also advocated a rapid shift to high‑altitude Himalayan solar energy to reduce reliance on vulnerable hydropower and improve resilience.

articles.title: Address the unique needs of women amid crisis
articles.summary: The government must take urgent action to address women's health, safety, and dignity during the current crisis.

articles.title: Flood sends hydropower shares tumbling, but damage is uneven
articles.summary: Severe flooding in the Bhotekoshi River basin has damaged several listed hydropower projects in Nepal, causing a sharp decline in the sector's stock prices. While the physical impact varies among plants, investors are reacting to uncertainty over the scale of losses, potential insurance claims, and the cost of reconstruction. The broader market, including insurance companies, also saw share prices fall as the financial community assesses the economic fallout of the disaster.

articles.title: People in flood-hit Rasuwa villages call for help after supplies run out
articles.summary: Residents of Aamachhodingmo Rural Municipality in Rasuwa, devastated by recent floods, are pleading for assistance as their emergency supplies have been exhausted. Many have lost family members and look to the sky for helicopters, but most of their prayers go unanswered.

articles.title: Mental wellbeing: How to help without feeling helpless after the floods
articles.summary: The article offers practical steps for coping with the emotional fallout of Nepal's recent floods. It suggests ways to contribute positively—such as donating to reputable charities, sharing verified information, and volunteering—while also emphasizing self‑care techniques like limiting exposure to distressing news, taking regular breaks, and seeking professional help when needed. By balancing outward assistance with personal mental health practices, readers can support flood‑affected communities without succumbing to feelings of helplessness.

articles.title: Iran to tackle economic issues, says further attacks will be ‘more painful’
articles.summary: Iran announced plans to implement economic reforms aimed at mitigating the impact of sanctions and war‑related pressures. Tehran warned that any further attacks on the country would provoke a faster and more damaging response, describing any such action as ‘more painful.’ The statement underscores Tehran’s intent to strengthen its economy while signaling a heightened willingness to retaliate against perceived aggression.

articles.title: Nepal moves against online abuse targeting flood survivors
articles.summary: The Nepal Cyber Bureau has set up a 10‑member team to track and identify users posting hateful and demeaning comments online about victims of the recent Bhotekoshi floods.

articles.title: Eight Indonesian airports remain shut due to volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau
articles.summary: Repeated eruptions of the Anak Krakatau volcano have spewed ash over Jakarta, forcing the closure of eight Indonesian airports. The ash cloud has led to widespread flight cancellations, affecting around 170,000 passengers, and prompted some schools in the region to shift to remote learning.

articles.title: Floods wash away 1,806 hectares of farmland, threaten food supplies
articles.summary: Heavy rains have caused the Bhotekoshi River to flood, washing away about 1,806 hectares of farmland across several districts in eastern Nepal. The inundation is projected to reduce food production by roughly 7,686 tonnes, raising concerns over local food security and the livelihoods of farming families. Authorities are assessing damage, coordinating relief efforts, and urging communities to prepare for possible further losses as the monsoon season continues.

articles.title: Arnold Dix says Nepal rescue teams face challenge unlike any before
articles.summary: Australian tunnel expert Arnold Dix arrived in Kathmandu and teamed up with Nepali and Indian rescue units to locate people believed to be trapped in the Chilime hydropower tunnel, describing the operation as an unprecedented challenge for Nepal’s emergency responders.

articles.title: Far-right AfD wins historic victory in German state election
articles.summary: The far‑right Alternative for Germany (AfD) secured a historic victory in a recent German state election, marking its strongest performance at the state level to date. The win intensifies pressure on Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s coalition government, as the AfD’s gains suggest a potential pathway to power that has not been seen since the Nazi era. Analysts warn that the result could reshape Germany’s political landscape and influence broader European right‑wing movements.
